## Natural history notes

A native perennial bunchgrass characterized by narrow leaves and distinctive twisting, three-branched awns that give the mature seedheads a corkscrew-like appearance. Corkscrew Threeawn occurs primarily in sandy, well-drained habitats, including scrub, sandhill, pine flatwoods, and open pine woodlands. Its native range is concentrated in the southeastern United States, particularly Florida and Georgia, and it is considered native and secure in South Florida. Like many grasses of Florida’s uplands, it is associated with open, disturbance- and fire-maintained plant communities.
